summary: FIX-MARKETWATCHER-EOD-OFFHOURS-SAMETICK-NOTEBOOK-COLLISION design complete. ROOT CAUSE: market-watcher-offhours (cron 0 */4 * * *) and market-watcher-eod (cron 0 16 * * 1-5) structurally collide every weekday at 16:00 UTC -- both spawn concurrently, both full-overwrite the SAME docs/agent-memory/notebooks/market-watcher.md. Independently re-verified this cycle (not the router's self-report): git log confirms market-watcher-eod's own 2026-08-14 16:00Z notebook entry is permanently lost (latest commit 23eed1755 is offhours' own write); commit 6cfdfb227 (message claims 'EOD notebook 2026-08-14 cycles 1') actually touched ONLY news-scout.md +7 lines -- a bare git_commit_retry with no trailing pathspec swept a concurrent peer's unrelated staged change into the wrong commit (RULE 2.5 / commit-mutex Step 2c PATHSPEC-SCOPED violation, confirmed live in both docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/eod.md Step D and cycle.md's offhours self-commit). The existing 2026-08-06 market-watcher-notebook:main task_claim mutex only guards the git-commit step, not the raw notebook Write() itself, so it cannot prevent this. FIX (brief SS3, PRIMARY): generalize the already-shipped, already-tested CHEF same-tick mutex (applyChefMutex / cowork-chef-mutex.js, live since FIX-COWORK-CHEF-SAMETICK-MUTEX 2026-06-30) into a new sibling pure function applySupersedeMutex (scripts/agents-flow/cowork-supersede-mutex.js), driven by a new declarative 'supersedes' field on the market-watcher-eod slot object in docs/data/cowork-schedule.json, wired unconditionally into cowork-match-slots.js's finish() right after applyChefMutex -- eliminates the double-spawn at the source, in-script (deterministic), not a flow-doc WARN an LLM dispatcher session might skip. FIX (brief SS4, SECONDARY fast-follow, router-flagged): add the missing trailing pathspec to both bare git_commit_retry calls in eod.md Step D and cycle.md's offhours self-commit -- independent defect, exposes market-watcher commits to ANY concurrently-committing peer, not just this pair. Brief SS5 explains why a split-notebook-file option and a write-level-mutex option were considered and rejected as primary (SS5 -- notebook is a real single-file consumer surface per fb-market-poster/flow/daily.md:102, and OVERWRITE-class semantics mean a write-mutex alone still loses content, just deterministically instead of racily). Brief SS6 flags a lower-severity residual risk (alert-commander-market/alert-commander-critical share the same collision SHAPE at 04:00/08:00 UTC, but alert-commander's notebook write is APPEND class, not OVERWRITE -- no action requested, awareness only).
